item.content:encoded:
I realize that the edits to cross-link this piece with 2935 were done back in 2016, but I have to point out that the world described by those that are effected by the item just appears empty or contaminated by something resembling an anomalous substance, but not really dead as described in 2935.

Besides that, the power was still working within 2935 when the agents arrived, they even just turned on a TV to show a burning shopping channel studio, but the areas explored by those using 201 describes it as more run down and empty, without even any bodies in the buildings or anything. Additionally, the way the "projects" are described, the power went out a long time ago, enough to make getting functioning devices powered even on a small scale difficult, which tells me that whatever happened, did so awhile ago.

Editing this, as if it had become "declassified":

In addition, reports of [DATA EXPUNGED]. It is unclear if these are real [DATA EXPUNGED]. Testing will commence if viable samples can be recovered.

In addition, reports of intermittent, fragmentary broadcasts have been returned by subjects attempting to repair power to media devices such as televisions and radios. It is unclear if these are real or the product of the degraded mental states of those remaining long enough to complete said projects, but reports consistently resemble automated messages prepared by the Foundation in contingency for XK-Class Scenarios. Testing will commence if viable samples can be recovered.

item.content:encoded:
There's some nostalgia factor for this one for a lot of people, but for me its the fridge horror of what it would be like to experience this:
It'd be sort of like of living out that feeling you get from games like Myst sometimes, where its just you, the sound of the wind, and a bunch of partially functional machinery. But this time there's no taking off the headphones for a minute to go hug your cat. In my headcanon, what's behind the expungments are sightings of human and inhuman entities ala Amnesia by test subjects who remain for long durations- those are removed because they don't know if they're real or if they're just hallucinations, on top of the fact that they don't know if this is some sort of real alternate universe or just a shared hypothetical reality.

BTW: I think I might like to throw my hat in the ring if this one ever comes up for an update/re-write. Have a nebulous idea forming for it.

Does the article author understand how large an area with a 40 meter radius is? I mean, that's almost two football fields, placed side by side. Also, I'm assuming that the contaminated area includes 40 meters above and below the object, so forget about containing it in a facility with multiple floors.

item.title: Re:
item.content:encoded:
1: All possible. The displacement effect is totally random, and there's no known "block" for it. Someone can get near it a hundred times and not get taken, other get snatched every time. Sometimes just one or two people out of a group, sometimes the whole thing. It just randomly "activates", truly luck of the draw.

2: Typically, with planned exposure, they are given some number to contact once they "come back", and fitted with some kind of tracking bug. However, in a lot of cases, it comes down to observation and monitoring. Some people may never get recovered, if they suddenly come back in a odd area.
